title: Overlap Attenuator: Adaptive Prefill Rate Controller with KV-prefetch Hysteresis
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: We observed intermittent 95/99p tail spikes during mixed prefill+decode workloads when continuous batching and KV cache priming competed for GPU and memory bandwidth. Motivation: Existing prefill throttlers oscillate when decode phases start early for short outputs, causing redundant KV prefetches and kernel thrash. This PR introduces an "overlap attenuator"—an adaptive prefill rate controller that smoothly dials back prefill issuance when decode progress is detected and gradually resumes prefill with hysteresis to avoid oscillation. Key ideas: 1) continuous-batch-aware kernel hints - scheduler annotates batches with a 'decode-likelihood' score derived from prefix length distribution and recent client TTLs; kernels get lightweight hints to prefer low-latency decode paths when score is high; 2) KV-prefetch hysteresis - prefetcher tracks a per-shard moving-window of decode handoffs and applies a hold-off timer plus exponential backoff to reduce wasted KV fetches when decode churn is present; 3) overlap attenuation - a controller that fuses kernel hints and KV-prefetch state to produce a single prefill-rate multiplier (0.0-1.0) per worker, applied to prefill admission and to the continuous batching connector; 4) safety fallbacks - instrumentation and hard caps to prevent starvation of prefill in rare pathological workloads. Implementation notes: - New module src/runtime/scheduler/overlap_attenuator.{cc,h} implements the control loop (C++). - Prefetch hysteresis added to src/runtime/kv/prefetcher.cc with lightweight per-shard state and backoff timers. - Scheduler emits 'decode-likelihood' in batch descriptors; kernel selection logic updated in src/runtime/kernel/selector.cc to accept hints. - Exposed runtime config flags: runtime.overlap_attenuator.enabled, runtime.overlap_attenuator.window_ms, runtime.kv.prefetch_hysteresis_ms, runtime.kv.prefetch_backoff_mult. - Added unit tests and simulation harness under tests/scheduler/attenuator_sim and e2e perf scenario in perf/benchmarks/overlap_attn_scenarios.yml. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-8873 linked) - [x] Unit tests covering controller transitions - [x] Integration test with continuous-batching enabled - [x] Benchmarks showing tail/throughput impact - [x] Feature flag gating for rollout - [x] Metrics and tracing added for observability Testing & results: - Synthetic mixed workload (50% short decode <16 tokens, 50% long prefill) on a 4xA100 cluster: 99p token latency down by 18ms (from 142ms -> 124ms), 95p down by 10ms. - Throughput change: <2% variance at 95% CL; improved end-to-end SLA stability observed. - KV prefetch traffic reduced by ~32% for the mixed workload, lowering host memory churn and NVMe reads in our tests. Rollout plan: will be rolled out as a staged canary behind runtime.overlap_attenuator.enabled: - stage 1: internal canary on dedicated-staging (10 nodes) - stage 2: 10% production traffic on a single region with feature flag - stage 3: global ramp to 100% with monitor dashboards and automatic rollback on spike in token errors or >10% tail regression Related work: this complements the speculative prefill experiments (ENG-9001) and provides a safer attenuator path for short-decode-heavy customers. Caveats and future work: - Current controller uses heuristics; future iteration will include learned thresholds from historical traffic and a ML-based chooser. - More aggressive KV eviction heuristics may be added when memory pressure is high.
